option_relations.rationale: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) is a potential cause of stroke, but it is not directly related to Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP).

Cardioembolic stroke with underlying hypercoagulable state due to metastatic breast cancer and autoimmune hemolytic anemia describes a complex etiology for stroke, but it is not directly related to Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP).
Thromboembolic stroke from hypercoagulable state describes a type of stroke and its general cause, but it is not directly related to Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP).
Trousseau’s syndrome (paraneoplastic hypercoagulability) is a specific hypercoagulable state, but it is not directly related to Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP).
